title: Track it right, test it fairly, launch it safely

say: Track it right, test it fairly, launch it safely.
This is the video for module two of Paid Advertising with Meta Ads.
Most failed campaigns are not killed by bad ads. They are killed by bad set-up: an ad account owned by someone who left, a Pixel that fires Purchase twice, or a card declined on day three.

panel.heading: Bad set-up kills more ads than bad ads
items: Account owned by a staff member who left

say: The business owner should own the business portfolio, the ad account and the Pixel. You are added as a partner, never given their password, and if you leave they keep everything.
Turn on two-factor authentication for everyone, with two trusted admins. Test the payment method, verify the Pixel and the domain, and set an account spending limit as a safety net.

panel.heading: Set-up and safety checklist
items: Portfolio owned by the client
Two-factor on, two admins
Payment method tested
Pixel and events verified
Domain verified
Spending limit set

say: The Meta Pixel is a small piece of code that sends events, like add to cart or purchase, to Meta. Open Test events, then browse your site. Each event should appear within seconds.

panel.heading: Check that your Pixel tells the truth
items: Open Test events in Events Manager
Browse, add to cart, start checkout
Check pages with Meta Pixel Helper
Place a real low-value test order
Add the Conversions API, same event ID

say: Check each page with the free Meta Pixel Helper on a laptop. Then place a real low-value test order and refund it.

say: Add the Conversions API, which sends the same events from the server and recovers ones the browser misses. Both must carry the same event ID, so Meta removes duplicates.

say: Halima's shop showed 40 purchases in Ads Manager, but only 22 real paid orders. Purchase was firing twice. After the fix, ROAS fell from an inflated 5.6 to a true 3.05.

panel.rule: Purchase fires once, with the right value and NGN.

say: Custom audiences are people who already know you. Retarget people who added to cart in the last 14 days but did not buy.

panel.heading: Give Meta the right signals
items: Retarget: added to cart, did not buy
Exclude existing customers from first-order ads
Lookalike from your best repeat buyers
Go broad once the Pixel has purchase history

say: And exclude existing customers, so you stop paying to show them first-order offers.

panel.heading: Give Meta the right signals
items: Retarget: added to cart, did not buy
Exclude existing customers from first-order ads
Lookalike from your best repeat buyers
Go broad once the Pixel has purchase history

say: A lookalike asks Meta to find people who resemble a source. It needs at least 100 people from one country, and your 600 best repeat customers beat 5,000 people who once liked a post. Uploading a customer list needs their consent.

say: Broad targeting works best once your Pixel has purchase history. But location stays a hard rule. If you only deliver in Lagos, set Lagos.

say: A test must change one thing only, start with a written hypothesis, have enough budget, and run for a fixed time. Ruth wants to test a demonstration video against a price-led carousel.

card.title: Is the budget big enough to test?

say: Purchases cost about 4,000 naira. For 30 per version she needs 60, which is 240,000 naira, about 17,100 a day over 14 days.

card.title: Is the budget big enough to test?

say: The client has only 8,000 naira a day. That buys just 14 purchases per version, too few to trust.

card.title: Is the budget big enough to test?

say: So she tests on add to cart instead, at about 900 naira each. That gives roughly 62 per version, then she confirms the winner on purchases later.

card.title: Is the budget big enough to test?

say: Read Meta's Advertising Standards for each client. Copy that implies you know something personal, like struggling with your weight, gets rejected. So do guaranteed health or beauty results, get-rich offers and fake buttons.

panel.heading: Rewrite it before Meta rejects it
right: Headline says what the ad is

say: Write: our programme helps people who. Keep claims honest, with NAFDAC registration where a product needs it. If it is a real breach, fix it, because repeated violations can restrict the whole ad account.

panel.heading: Rewrite it before Meta rejects it

say: Run your pre-launch check on a phone every time. Then in the first hours, check only for faults: is it delivering, is spend on track, any rejections?

panel.heading: Monitor early, decide later
items: Hour 2: is it delivering?
Day 1: spend and errors
Days 2 to 7: hands off
Day 7: compare with target CPA
Day 14: decisions

say: Leave it alone during learning. From day 7, compare each ad set with your target cost per sale. Watch for creative fatigue: frequency climbing while clicks fall. The fix is new creative.

say: When an ad set beats target, raise its budget in modest steps, not double. Write every change in a change log, with the date and reason, and send a plain weekly report that leads with orders, revenue and cost per order.

panel.rule: Raise winning budgets about 20 percent at a time.

say: To remember. The client owns every asset. Verify that Purchase fires once. Use custom audiences to retarget and exclude. Test one variable with enough events. And check every launch on a phone, and log every change.

One variable, enough events, fixed dates

say: Now practise. Set up and verify a Pixel on a practice site and record what fires. Design an audience and test plan with a budget calculation. Then build your reusable QA checklist, naming system, change log and report template.
